lock.title: How Mutex::lock works
lock.description: Gives one thread at a time access to the data inside.

slides.caption: lock() waits until no other thread holds the lock, then lends the data. The lock is released when the guard is dropped.
B was waiting; now it locks and adds 1.
C does the same. No update is lost.
lock() returns a Result because a thread that panicked while holding the lock "poisons" it.

channel.title: How mpsc::channel works
channel.description: Creates a channel: a Sender for one side and a Receiver for the other.

slides.caption: Values sent into tx come out of rx, in the same order.
mpsc means many producers, one consumer: clone tx to send from several threads.

send.title: How Sender::send works
send.description: Puts a value into the channel; it moves to the receiving side.

slides.caption: send never waits for the receiver (the channel has room for any number of values).
"a" is sent and now belongs to the channel.
"b" is sent from another thread through a cloned Sender.
send returns Err if the Receiver no longer exists.

recv.title: How Receiver::recv works
recv.description: Waits for the next value; Err once every Sender is gone.

slides.caption: recv blocks until a value arrives.
All Senders were dropped and the channel is empty: Err, and the loop ends.
for x in rx { ... } does the same thing. try_recv() never waits.

new.title: How Mutex::new works
new.description: Wraps data so only one thread at a time can use it.

slides.caption: The data lives inside the Mutex; the only way in is lock().
Share it between threads with Arc<Mutex<T>>.

try_lock.title: How Mutex::try_lock works
try_lock.description: Locks if free right now; never waits.

slides.caption: lock() waits; try_lock() gives up at once if someone else holds the lock.
Useful to avoid deadlocks, or to skip work when a resource is busy.

into_inner.title: How Mutex::into_inner works
into_inner.description: Takes the data out of the Mutex for good.

slides.caption: Owning the Mutex means no other thread can use it, so no locking is needed.
With Arc<Mutex<T>>, first get the Mutex back with Arc::into_inner.

get_mut.title: How Mutex::get_mut works
get_mut.description: Direct &mut access when you own the Mutex exclusively.

slides.caption: &mut Mutex already proves nobody else is using it.

is_poisoned.title: How Mutex::is_poisoned works
is_poisoned.description: true if a thread panicked while holding the lock.

slides.caption: A panic while locked "poisons" the Mutex, warning that the data might be inconsistent.
A thread panicked holding the lock: true.
lock() then returns Err(PoisonError); into_inner() on that error still gives the data.

read.title: How RwLock::read works
read.description: Shared read access: many readers at once.

note.text: readers do not block each other

slides.caption: An RwLock allows many readers or one writer.
Reader 2 too, at the same time.
Good for data that is read often and changed rarely, like configuration.

write.title: How RwLock::write works
write.description: Exclusive write access: waits until no readers or writers remain.

slides.caption: write() blocks new readers and waits for current ones to finish.
1 is pushed; the guard drops at the end of the line.
Holding a read guard and calling write() on the same thread deadlocks.

try_read.title: How RwLock::try_read works
try_read.description: Reads if possible right now; never waits.

slides.caption: Fails at once while a writer holds the lock.
A write guard is alive: Err.

get_or_init.title: How OnceLock::get_or_init works
get_or_init.description: Initialises a value exactly once, even with many threads racing.

slides.caption: The first caller runs the closure; everyone else gets the same stored value.
B gets the stored value; the closure never runs twice.
static CONFIG: OnceLock<Config> = OnceLock::new(); is the classic use.

set.title: How OnceLock::set works
set.description: Fills the OnceLock if empty; otherwise returns your value in Err.

slides.caption: get() returns Some only after a successful set.

force.title: How LazyLock works
force.description: A global value computed on first use, safely across threads.

slides.caption: Statics must be constant; LazyLock lets them hold computed values like a Vec or a HashMap.
The first access runs the closure.
Every later access, from any thread, sees the same Vec.
Replaces the older lazy_static! and once_cell crates.

call_once.title: How Once::call_once works
call_once.description: Runs a piece of code only the first time, no matter how often it is called.

slides.caption: Once remembers that it has run.
The first call runs the closure.
OnceLock is usually nicer, because it also stores a value.

wait.title: How Barrier::wait works
wait.description: Makes threads wait until all of them have arrived.

slides.caption: Each thread blocks in wait() until the third one arrives.
Thread 3 arrives: all three continue together.
Exactly one thread gets is_leader() == true, handy for one-time work after the barrier.

sync_channel.title: How mpsc::sync_channel works
sync_channel.description: A channel with a fixed capacity: send waits when it is full.

slides.caption: A bounded channel stops a fast producer from running far ahead of the consumer.
The channel is full: send would wait, try_send fails.
sync_channel(0) makes every send wait for a matching recv (a rendezvous).

try_recv.title: How Receiver::try_recv works
try_recv.description: Takes a value if one is waiting; never blocks.

slides.caption: Good for game loops: handle all pending messages, then draw a frame.

recv_timeout.title: How Receiver::recv_timeout works
recv_timeout.description: Waits for a value, but only up to a time limit.

slides.caption: recv waits forever; recv_timeout gives up after the duration.
Lets a worker wake up regularly to check a stop flag.

try_iter.title: How Receiver::try_iter works
try_iter.description: An iterator over the values already waiting, without blocking.

slides.caption: try_iter stops as soon as the channel is empty, even if Senders still exist.
They are collected; then it stops.
iter() would instead wait for more until every Sender is gone.

condvar-new.title: How Condvar::new works
condvar-new.description: A condition variable: lets threads sleep until another thread signals a change.

slides.caption: The Mutex guards the data; the Condvar is the doorbell.
A flag protected by a Mutex.
A Condvar to signal when it changes.
Waiting threads use no CPU while asleep.

condvar-wait.title: How Condvar::wait works
condvar-wait.description: Releases the lock and sleeps until notified, then re-locks.

l3.text: wake up, lock again: ready = true

slides.caption: Spurious wake-ups can happen, so the condition is checked again in a loop.
Check the flag under the lock.
wait gives up the lock while sleeping.
Another thread changes the flag and notifies.
wait returns with the lock held again.
wait_while writes the loop for you.

wait_while.title: How Condvar::wait_while works
wait_while.description: Waits as long as a condition holds, re-checking after every wake-up.

slides.caption: A producer pushes and notifies: wake up.
Change the data under the lock first, then notify.
Each woken thread re-checks the condition under the lock.
Use it when the change matters to everyone.

wait_timeout.title: How Condvar::wait_timeout works
wait_timeout.description: Waits for a notification, but only up to a time limit.

slides.caption: Returns the guard and whether the time ran out.
Still check your condition: a notification may have arrived just in time.

wait_timeout_while.title: How Condvar::wait_timeout_while works
wait_timeout_while.description: Waits while a condition holds, up to a time limit.

slides.caption: Good for "wait up to 5 seconds for the worker".

note.text: result: timed out: true, flag: false

timed_out.title: How WaitTimeoutResult::timed_out works
timed_out.description: true if a timed wait ended because time ran out.

slides.caption: Tells timeouts apart from real notifications.

once-new.title: How Once::new works
once-new.description: A flag for code that must run only one time.

is_completed.title: How Once::is_completed works
is_completed.description: true once call_once has finished successfully.

slides.caption: A quick check without running anything.
A panic inside call_once leaves it false (poisoned).

call_once_force.title: How Once::call_once_force works
call_once_force.description: Like call_once, but also runs if an earlier attempt panicked.

slides.caption: The closure is told whether a previous attempt failed.
call_once would panic on a poisoned Once.

once_state-is_poisoned.title: How OnceState::is_poisoned works
once_state-is_poisoned.description: Inside call_once_force: did a previous attempt panic?

slides.caption: On a first, clean run it is false.
true means you may need to clean up first.

once-wait.title: How Once::wait works
once-wait.description: Blocks until another thread has completed the Once.

slides.caption: B does not run the setup itself; it just waits for it.
B returns from wait once it is done.
Panics if the Once was poisoned; wait_force does not.
Fill it later with set or get_or_init.

get.title: How OnceLock::get works
get.description: The value if it was set, otherwise None; never waits.

slides.caption: wait() blocks until it is set.

oncelock-get_mut.title: How OnceLock::get_mut works
oncelock-get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the value, with exclusive access.

slides.caption: Only possible when nobody else can see the lock.
None if it was never set.

take.title: How OnceLock::take works
take.description: Takes the value out, leaving the lock empty.

slides.caption: The lock can be set again.

oncelock-into_inner.title: How OnceLock::into_inner works
oncelock-into_inner.description: Unwraps the lock: Some(value) if it was set.

oncelock-wait.title: How OnceLock::wait works
oncelock-wait.description: Blocks until another thread sets the value, then returns it.

slides.caption: Unlike get, it does not return None while empty.
Never returns if nobody ever sets it.

lazylock-new.title: How LazyLock::new works
lazylock-new.description: A thread-safe value computed on first use.

slides.caption: Statics can hold computed values this way.

force_mut.title: How LazyLock::force_mut works
force_mut.description: Initialises if needed and gives &mut to the value.

slides.caption: For a local LazyLock you own.

lazylock-get_mut.title: How LazyLock::get_mut works
lazylock-get_mut.description: A mutable reference to the value if it is already initialised.

slides.caption: Unlike force_mut, it never runs the closure.

rwlock-new.title: How RwLock::new works
rwlock-new.description: Wraps data so many threads can read or one can write.

slides.caption: read() for shared access, write() for exclusive access.

try_write.title: How RwLock::try_write works
try_write.description: Takes the write lock if it is free right now; never waits.

slides.caption: Fails while any reader or writer holds the lock.

rwlock-into_inner.title: How RwLock::into_inner works
rwlock-into_inner.description: Takes the data out of the RwLock.

slides.caption: Owning the lock means nobody else is using it.

rwlock-get_mut.title: How RwLock::get_mut works
rwlock-get_mut.description: Direct &mut access when you own the RwLock exclusively.

rwlock-is_poisoned.title: How RwLock::is_poisoned works
rwlock-is_poisoned.description: true if a writer panicked while holding the lock.

slides.caption: Only a panic during write poisons it; readers do not.
clear_poison resets it once you have fixed the data.

clear_poison.title: How RwLock::clear_poison works
clear_poison.description: Marks a poisoned RwLock as healthy again.

slides.caption: Call it once you know the data is consistent.
Mutex::clear_poison does the same for a Mutex.

mutex-clear_poison.title: How Mutex::clear_poison works
mutex-clear_poison.description: Marks a poisoned Mutex as healthy again.

slides.caption: Only clear it once the data is known to be valid.

poison_error-into_inner.title: How PoisonError::into_inner works
poison_error-into_inner.description: Gets the guard anyway from a poisoned lock.

slides.caption: The data is still there; poisoning is only a warning.
A common pattern when a panic cannot leave the data broken.

get_ref.title: How PoisonError::get_ref works
get_ref.description: Looks at the guarded data inside a poisoning error.

slides.caption: Inspect the data before deciding what to do.

poison_error-get_mut.title: How PoisonError::get_mut works
poison_error-get_mut.description: Mutable access to the guarded data inside a poisoning error.

slides.caption: into_inner takes the guard out instead.

poison_error-new.title: How PoisonError::new works
poison_error-new.description: Wraps a value in a PoisonError, for your own lock types.

slides.caption: Lets custom synchronisation types report poisoning like std does.

barrier-new.title: How Barrier::new works
barrier-new.description: A meeting point for n threads.

slides.caption: Each thread calls wait(); all continue when the n-th arrives.
The barrier can be reused for the next round.

is_leader.title: How BarrierWaitResult::is_leader works
is_leader.description: true for exactly one of the threads released by a barrier.

slides.caption: Handy for one-time work after everyone arrives.
One of them is the leader.
Which thread is leader is not specified.

sync_sender-send.title: How SyncSender::send works
sync_sender-send.description: Sends a value, waiting if the bounded channel is full.

title.text: tx.send(1)?; tx.send(2)?;   // second waits for a recv

slides.caption: With a full channel, send blocks until the receiver makes room.

try_send.title: How SyncSender::try_send works
try_send.description: Sends if there is room right now; otherwise returns the value in an error.

slides.caption: The value is given back so nothing is lost.
Disconnected means the receiver is gone.

iter.title: How Receiver::iter works
iter.description: An iterator that waits for each value and ends when every Sender is gone.

slides.caption: The loop stops by itself once no more values can arrive.
The sender is dropped: the loop ends.
for msg in rx works the same way.

lazylock-get.title: How LazyLock::get works
lazylock-get.description: The value if already computed; never runs the closure.

wait_force.title: How Once::wait_force works
wait_force.description: Blocks until the Once has run, even if a previous run panicked.

slides.caption: wait() would panic on a poisoned Once; wait_force does not.

downgrade.title: How RwLockWriteGuard::downgrade works
downgrade.description: Turns a write lock into a read lock without letting another writer in between.

slides.caption: Other readers may join right away; no writer can sneak in.
Dropping and re-locking would leave a gap.
